rule.borderline_note: Rows flagged borderline are the ones where the two readings genuinely compete. Every one carries the reasoning that decided it, so a human can flip it and rerun.
rule.not_scheme: the money runs, builds, staffs or maintains an organisation or an asset (college, hospital, directorate, board, corporation, building, vehicle, office), devolves general purpose funds to another tier of government, or is an accounting or adjustment head
rule.scheme: the money buys an identifiable benefit received by a person or household: cash, kit, food, scholarship, fee waiver, pension, insurance, subsidy, loan, free travel, a house, treatment for a named beneficiary class, or training given to people

sampling: Stratified by book (SCSP/TSP, else Child, else Gender) crossed with allocation band (none, and quartiles of the 865 rows that carry an allocation), 15 strata. Within a stratum rows are sorted by head of account and picked at even spacing, so the sample is reproducible without a random seed. Allocation is proportional to stratum size with a floor of 4, so the sample is close to self weighting; stratum_size and stratum_sampled are carried on every row so a weighted estimate can be recomputed.

audit.what: Every row the classifier calls a scheme at score 5 or above that the stratified sample had not already covered. Together the two sets are a census of the published region, so the published list's precision is counted rather than estimated. The audit was made after the weights were fixed and was not fed back into them.

stratified.what: A probability sample of all 969 rows. This is the only set the threshold sweep uses, because precision and recall estimated on anything else would not generalise to the rows the classifier has not seen.

what: Hand labels for a stratified sample of Karnataka's scheme-wise budget rows. Ground truth for parse/classify_karnataka.py. Audit and correct these: the classifier is only as good as they are.
